triples.relationship: prophetic words associated with realized judgment
triples.rationale: Zechariah calls for receiving God's words and ordinances given through the prophets and records acknowledgment that the Lord acted according to the people's ways. Chronicles describes deportation and desolation as fulfilling the Lord's word through Jeremiah. Both connect the people's experience of judgment with the prophetic word.
triples.source_text: Yet receive My words and My ordinances, all that I, in My Spirit, command My servants the prophets, who overtook your fathers.” And they answered and said, “As the Lord Almighty has arrayed Himself to act according to your ways and practices, so He acted toward you.”

target_units.text: He deported the survivors to Babylon, and they became slaves to him and his sons until the kingdom of the Medes,
to fulfill the Lord’s word through Jeremiah’s mouth, until the land accepted its Sabbaths, to keep Sabbath. All the days of its desolation it kept Sabbath, to complete seventy years.

triples.relationship: wages that fail to benefit the workers
triples.rationale: Zechariah describes a period when people's wages will bring no benefit. Haggai likewise pictures earned wages gathered into a bundle with holes among the people's frustrated efforts. Both specifically describe ineffective wages in the rebuilding setting.
triples.source_text: Before those days people’s wages will bring no benefit, and animals’ hire will not exist; those going out or coming in will have no peace because of affliction. I will send everyone out against his neighbor.

target_units.text: You sowed much and brought in little; you ate, but were not satisfied; you drank, but not to intoxication; you clothed yourselves, but were not warmed in them. The one gathering wages gathered them into a bundle with holes.
